.

【簽證資訊】
Please be aware of our disposition at UC Chile regarding the migratory procedures which must be carried out by students in mobility to Chile, in accordance with the new Chilean migratory law (Ley No. 21,325).
Those students coming to Chile for a period of less than 180 days may enter the country under a permit called 'Permiso de Permanencia Transitoria', which is granted automatically* when you enter the country. It is applicable to short stays including tourism and study purposes, among others. It has a duration of 90 days and it is renewable for an additional 90-day period by lodging a visa extension (prórroga de Permanencia Transitoria).
Important: Citizens from some countries are required to apply beforehand for the ´Permiso de Permanencia Transitoria: Check first the column 'REQ. VISTUR' at
this link
and if you are subject to apply for this permit you can lodge your application following the instructions contained at the
Official Website
from The Chilean Ministry of Foreign Affairs, 'Servicios Consulares' (in Spanish).
Those students coming to Chile for a period longer than 180 days must apply for a Temporary Visa (Residencia Temporal, under subclass 'student') through the
Official Website
of the Chilean National Migration Service.
【住宿資訊】

The University does not have any type of student dormitories or residencies nor coordinates housing for international students.

【住宿資訊】
不保證住宿
，詳情請參閱以下資訊：
Students are welcome to apply for on-campus housing regardless of the term they are attending Cornell; however, be aware that on-campus housing is limited and not guaranteed.
Fall semester:
Finding housing can be very challenging.
On-campus housing
is not available, and single-semester leases within commuting distance are difficult to secure.
Spring semester:
Housing may be available on-campus and is generally easy to find off-campus.
Academic year:
Off-campus
only
Note: Upon nomination to Cornell we encourage students to begin searching for housing. However, students should not commit to housing (financially or otherwise) until they have received admission notification from Cornell and have secured a visa appointment.

【住宿資訊】
保證住宿
，住宿資訊請參考
此連結
On-campus housing is guaranteed for all exchange students that
complete the online housing application by the due date
.
We recommend that all exchange students live on campus in residence halls. On-campus living is an important part of American university life, and by living on campus, you become an active member of the UConn community and have access to all the social, recreational, and cultural events that take place.
All dorm rooms are equipped with a bed, a mattress, a desk and chair, and a closet. In small units, doubles are 154 sq. ft. (11×14). Elsewhere, double rooms range in size up to 180 sq. ft. Most undergraduate dormitory rooms share bathroom facilities with other residents on the floor. Refrigerators, microwaves and televisions are not provided in dorm rooms.
Traditional Housing
– Shared bedrooms with convenient access to dining halls and campus facilities. A
campus meal plan
is required.
Suites
– Shared bedrooms, often with shared living spaces, with convenient access to dining halls and campus facilities. A
campus meal plan
is required.
Apartments
– Independent-style housing that has shared bedrooms and living spaces (including full kitchens). You are NOT required to have a campus meal plan.

Exchange students can be placed anywhere on-campus and usually live in the Quads, Carolina International House at Maxcy College (Maxcy), Bates-West or any of the Horseshoe apartments.
Housing is guaranteed but preferences are not.

【住宿資訊】
不保證住宿

此連結
On-campus housing
is NOT guaranteed
, but our office will run a first come, first served housing interest list before sending the list over to ASU Housing. Students are not recommended to apply to on-campus housing without being approved by our office first. If students are too late/do not get a space in on-campus housing through our office, they are encouraged to find off-campus housing asap.
Housing Price Increase (as at July 2026)
The state of Arizona is experiencing a sharp increase in average rent costs, in Tempe especially. Students can expect to pay between $6,000 USD to $9,000 USD (approximately) for housing in spring.
On-campus housing
does have costs between $5,000 USD (shared bedroom) - $12,000 USD (single bedroom apartment), but on-campus housing is extremely limited.  Students can find more information
here
.

【選課限制】
欲選填該校為志願的同學，請務必先行詳閱系所限制，自行確認是否有足夠課程可供選讀、是否符合申請資格，以及是否具備相關領域之背景知識：
Academic Program Restrictions
Engineering Enrollment Restrictions
The following schools in engineering have further enrollment restrictions for engineering students:
Computing, Informatics, and Decision Systems Engineering:
Students can request course overrides if they meet the prerequisites.  If a course is close to capacity, students may need to wait until closer to the start of the semester to receive an override.
Sustainable Engineering and the Built Environment:
If there are a large number of open seats, students will be allowed to enroll in courses for which they meet prerequisites.  If there are very few seats available, advisors will wait until 1-2 weeks before the start of the semester before giving permission for exchange students to enroll.
Engineering of Matter, Transport, and Energy:
After all registration has opened, students may be given overrides into courses that still have a lot of seats open, depending on the course demand for ASU majors.  For these courses, advisers will wait until the FIRST WEEK of the semester before giving permission for exchange students to enroll.
Warning – Extreme Course Limitation
: The following ASU engineering disciplines
cannot guarantee
exact course enrollment. This will cause incoming exchange students to fall off track and possibly delay their home university graduation.
Aerospace Engineering
Chemical Engineering
Materials Science and Engineering
Mechanical Engineering
Solar Energy Engineering and Commercialization
Civil, Environmental and Sustainable Engineering
Construction Engineering
Construction Management
Non-Engineering Enrollment Restrictions
W.P. Carey School of Business (undergraduate programs)
: seats are limited depending on the specific academic unit or course; one example is Supply Chain Management (SCM) which has extremely limited spaces for exchange students.
W.P. Carey School of Business (MBA)
: prior approval required during exchange program nomination phase (limited course offerings)
Engineering of Matter, Transport, and Energy:
After all registration has opened, students may be given overrides into courses that still have a lot of seats open, depending on the course demand for ASU majors. For these courses, advisers will wait until the FIRST WEEK of the semester before giving permission for exchange students to enroll.
Walter Cronkite School of Journalism & Mass Comm:
JMC courses are not available; MCO courses are limited. Alternative courses in other colleges may be found under the following prefixes: COM & ENG
College of Health Solutions:
seats are limited depending on the specific academic unit or course
Edson College of Nursing and Health Innovation:
most courses are restricted
Sandra Day O’Connor College of Law:
graduate-level courses are only available to graduate-level law students; undergraduate courses are available to all other exchange students
Mary Lou Fulton Teacher’s College:
most courses are restricted

【住宿資訊】
保證住宿
，更多資訊請見
此連結
Undergraduate students should be able to secure housing as long as they complete the online housing application on the
Department of Resident Life
website.
Full-year students sign an academic year lease and may not move out of on-campus housing at the change of the semester.
Housing fees depend on the type of housing that is assigned.
Some on-campus accommodations do not have kitchen facilities. In these cases, students are required to purchase a dining plan and do not have the option of waiving out of an on-campus dining plan.
Students who are assigned to on-campus accommodations with a kitchen can opt out of a dining plan.

【ELI Courses】
If the student's English test score is below the level required to waive the ELI Placement Test and they do not qualify for an exemption, the student must take the ELI Placement test before the semester starts. This is mandatory. Depending on the ELI Placement Test results, the student may be placed into 1 to 3 ELI classes (intermediate or advanced). These classes will be taken with their other university courses.
Does the "three ELI courses" refer to a total of three classes for the semester, or are they a semester-long course that counts for credits?
Depending on ELI Placement test results, the student may be required to enroll in 1-3 ELI classes. Each ELI class has lectures throughout the semester. Here is information on what they can expect from the ELI courses: https://www.hawaii.edu/eli/courses/eli-courses/
If it's a semester-long course, how many credits does it count for? And is it included in the minimum 8 credits and maximum 16 credits required for graduate studies?
Each ELI course is the equivalent of 3 credits for registration and U.S. immigration enrollment requirements for F-1 students. However, any ELI courses numbered below 100 count as 0 credits on the final transcript report and may not be considered transferable back to their home university. Please find more information on the credit policy here: https://www.hawaii.edu/eli/courses/credit/
If the three courses exceed 8 credits, can I simply take the ELI courses and skip the other courses?
If the student wants to do that, it's fine with us. However it may mean that they have no academic credit transferable back to their home university. The grades on their transcript would appear as "CR" for credit received or "NC" for no credit but will not indicate any GPA.

【住宿資訊】
不保證住宿
，住宿資訊請參考下方說明：
Incoming exchange students are encouraged to live in campus-owned residences. Housing charges are billed per semester.
OU Housing and Food Services
offers two
choices
to exchange students who want to live on the Norman campus: OU Traditions Square or Kraettli Apartments.
While OU cannot guarantee on-campus housing for all exchange students, every effort will be made to house exchange students on campus who meet the deadlines communicated to them by the Exchange Student Coordinator. Most incoming exchange students obtain housing on campus if they meet the deadlines. The Office of International Student Services manages on-campus housing requests for exchange students. Exchange students should NOT apply for housing through the regular OU Housing and Food Services website. All questions about on-campus housing for exchange students should be directed to the Exchange Student Coordinator.

All campuses operate on the semester system,

steps.summary: 不得自行延長、縮短或變更身分；須依合作校課程及學分規定。
details: 不得自行延長、縮短或變更身分；須依合作校課程及學分規定。

【學校年曆】
A UC full academic year includes 30 weeks of instruction:
Three quarters (UC Davis, UC Irvine, UC Los Angeles, UC Riverside, UC Santa Cruz, UC Santa Barbara and UC San Diego) or
Two semesters (UC Berkeley and UC Merced)
A UC quarter is 10 weeks of instruction (UC Davis, UC Irvine, UC Los Angeles, UC Riverside, UC Santa Cruz, UC Santa Barbara and UC San Diego):
Fall quarter (mid-September - mid-December)
Winter quarter (January - mid-March)
Spring quarter (April - mid-June)
A UC semester is 15 weeks of instruction (UC Berkeley and UC Merced):
Fall semester (mid-August - mid-December)
Spring semester (mid-January - mid-May)
Before making travel plans, verify the mandatory orientation date at your host UC. We strongly advise that you
do not
make personal financial commitments, including but not limited to purchasing tickets/insurance or reserving accommodations, until you receive your DS-2019 for the visa application, confirm your consular appointment and are granted a student visa.
各校區學年行事曆請參考
UC Academic Calendar
各年度第一學期甄選為August/September Arrival
Berkeley及Merced校區為Fall Semester 或 Fall Semester and Spring Semester
其餘校區為Fall Quarter only 或 Fall Quarter, Winter Quarter and Spring Quarter
各年度第二學期甄選為January Arrival
Berkeley及Merced校區為Spring Semester only
其餘校區為Winter Quarter only
【選課限制】
申請本計畫請先至各校區網站查詢該校是否有符合在本校就讀科系之相關領域，以免申請被拒或被分發至其他領域。請參考
UCEAP網頁
，主動確認目前就讀之科系在UCEAP各校區中可以申請
部分課程要求提供已修畢之先修課程證明（成績單），請同學務必遵守規定，切勿草率選課
如有同時參與研究計畫，或有減修需求，請務必事先告知NTU Study Abroad及UCEAP並獲得許可
If a student is specializing in two majors at the home university, the student must decide which major will be a priority while at UC.
If a student is applying to one of the
popular UC majors
, a student must be enrolled in a similar field of study at the home university.
Academic workload: Minimum of
12 units per academic term
; 13 units per academic term required at most UCB colleges. Most UC students enroll in 14-17 units per term.
In the UC system,
biology, business administration, economics, engineering, and psychology require intensive preparation for coursework taught at the upper-division level (100-199).
To be approved for upper-division courses, you must demonstrate to UC departmental advisors and/or instructors that you are sufficiently prepared.
NOT ALL MAJORS ARE OPEN TO RECIPROCITY STUDENTS
Use the
search tool
to explore UC majors. Majors are listed under the discipline with which they are most often associated. Some majors that have restricted enrollment are not open to reciprocity students and will not appear in your search and the majors below are
not
available.
BUSINESS ADMINISTRATION (MBA PROGRAMS)
Except by special arrangement with selected partner schools, MBA courses are not open to reciprocity students.
DESIGN
MEDICINE, NURSING, VETERINARY MEDICINE
Medical education is taught in graduate schools which are not open to reciprocity students. If you are an undergraduate interested in these areas of study, see biology at all campuses and animal science at UC Davis.
LAW
Law school courses are not open to reciprocity students.  See legal studies course for an introduction to the American legal system.  See also complementary courses in political science, international relations, global studies and sociology.

One on-campus and six off-campus International Houses of Kyoto University, and other dormitories are offered for international students.
Application period starts around three months before their arrival. Students should apply by themselves with their own preferences through online system. Monthly rent is around 100-400 US Dollars.
There are one on-campus and five off-campus International Houses of Kyoto University and other dormitories offered for exchange students. However, they are not guaranteed and are subject to availability due to limited housing capacity. As of Fall 2023, 70% of the exchange students were allocated a dorm room on a lottery-basis. We would appreciate your kind understanding on this matter.

【保險資訊】
Exchange students or their parents/guardians are responsible for the cost of any medical treatment should it arise during their stay in Korea and HUFS. Students should bring comprehensive travel and medical insurance before coming to Korea which covers hospitalization and medical care occurring during international travel and sojourns, as well as repatriation to their home country in any case of medical emergency.
Additionally, starting Spring 2021, a new law requires all exchange students to register and pay for the National Health Insurance plan in Korea. This is a monthly payment that helps medical and health expenses and services in Korea. Students can apply for an exemption from this healthcare after they arrive in Korea.

details: 住宿無保證；保險、役男出境與註冊依官方要求。

【保險資訊】
All international students in Korea are subject to mandatory enrollment in the National Health Insurance Service (NHIS) while in Korea. The estimated cost is approximately KRW 75,490 (USD $60) per month. Once enrolled, students will receive various benefits, including dental, traditional Korean medicinal treatment, health exams and check-ups, and pregnancy and other childbirth-related medical coverage, just as Korean citizens receive.
【住宿資訊】
Students can apply for on-campus housing to be assigned to a shared room in one of several on-campus dormitories. The dormitory fee for one semester can range from around USD $500 to $1,000, depending on the meal plan (which is optional). This application should be completed separately by online application before the start of the semester.

【生活費與保險資訊】
On average, exchange students spend approximately 800,000~1,500,000 KRW/month. This depends on their accommodation, lifestyle, and many other factors. In a rough estimate, 12,000 KRW/meal, 5,000KRW/coffee, 1,600KRW/ride public transit, etc.
Students must obtain overseas insurance BEFORE entering Korea. After the arrival in Korea, students will be OBLIGED to obtain the National Health Insurance (Monthly fee: approx. KRW72,000)

不保證住宿，住宿資訊請參考以下網頁
Seoul campus
Global campus

It is mandatory for students to obtain health insurance. Students may obtain their insurance at their home country or through Ewha Womans University. ※ Cost of Ewha Collective Insurance: 42,000 KRW per semester and 60,000 KRW per year (Fees are subject to change). Students will need to obtain all necessary insurance to study in Korea.

details: 住宿無保證；保險、役男出境與註冊依官方要求。

【住宿與其他資訊】
学费:根据两校协议,公费生免除接收学校的学费。
保险:交换生需在离境前自行于当地购买境外保险(含人身意外险,紧急救援险,住院医疗险),以涵盖交换期间一切医疗及意外支出,并将电子版发往或到校后交至我校。
住宿:校内住宿,本科宿舍为标准四人间配备,上床下桌,实现空调、热水器、独立卫生间全覆盖,设有洗衣房、自动
贩售机、咖啡机、直饮水等设施供学生日常使用。根据房型住宿费约为人民币500-700元/学期,床上用品需自行购买,
上网费,热水、电费等据实结算。
接送机服务:提供接送机服务,费用由我校承担。
所有课程以中文普通话教学
来校后交换生有机会参加丰富的交流活动，融入校园和当地
【保險與生活費資訊】
生活费：约人民币1000-1500元/月，依生活消费习惯各异
港澳台校際交流學生目前暫未納入基本醫療保險範圍，學生來校前應自行購買相關健康及意外傷害保險。
交换生需在离境前自行于当地购买境外保险（含人身意外险，紧急救援险，住院医疗险），以涵盖交换期间一切医疗及意外支出，并将电子版发往或到校后交至我校。

details: 住宿無保證；保險、役男出境與註冊依官方要求。

【住宿資訊】
住宿費：
學生可入住東南大學學生公寓，公寓分佈於三個校區，規格不同，雙人間(專為海外學生準備)每學期2400-4500元/床不等；四人間(學生宿舍)每學期900-1200元/床不等(不含床上用品床墊2個、床單2床、棉被2床、枕心1只、枕套2個、席子1床、蚊帳1頂，費用大約600左右人民幣)；
宿舍一般是四人一間。儘量安排與自己同專業的東大學生共住，便於交流。
床上用品可委託東南大學提供，四人間每學期900-1200元/床位費不等(不含床上用品床墊2個、床單2床、棉被2床、枕心1只、枕套2個、席子1床、蚊帳1頂，大約600元人民幣)。另外還有海外學院提供的宿舍，每月2400－4500元人民幣不等。
水、電超額部分需自付。請不要使用大功率的電器。
衛浴設施的情況有兩種根據不同標準而訂。一是，四牌樓同一樓層的人共用，設在宿舍間外。二是，同宿舍的共用，設在宿舍間內。

【保險及生活費資訊】
保險：交換生須提前購買人身意外傷害保險。
生活花費：估計1500 人民幣 / 月。
【住宿及其他資訊】
宿舍：由校方安排。每間宿舍2-4人，根據當年入住情況安排。宿舍配有床、空調、衣櫃、鞋櫃、書桌等基本設施，其他個人生活用品需學生自行準備。
南京物價水準：平均每月基本個人花費為人民幣1500元左右。
學伴：每學期從南京大學在校生中招募同學作為交換生的學伴,相伴一學期,協助交換生更好、更快地適應南大的交流學習生活,讓你的南大之行更加豐富多彩。
每學期將舉辦入學說明會、校園導覽、入學歡迎晚宴、國情考察活動、傳統節假日慶祝活動、期末分享會、歡送晚宴以及不定期舉行的各類豐富多彩交流體驗活動。

【住宿、體檢、保險..等資訊】
Q：校内宿舍是否需要自行预定？
A：不需要。校内交换生统一住在校内本地学生的公寓楼中，一般为四人间。学校在同学录取之后会代为为同学们安排住房，在入校后即可办理入住。
Q：学校要求的体检需要包含什么项目？
A：学校认可当地(台灣)正规体检机构的体检报告，按当地体检机构的要求进行体检即可，在当地附属院校的医疗机构或正式体检机构检查均可，项目需涵盖血液常规、胸透、传染病史等基本项目且报告时间需在最近 6 个月之内。
Q：提交的保险证明需涵盖哪些内容？
A：建议同学们购买的保险需涵盖往返交通、在大陆/内地期间的门诊、急诊、意外伤害等基本项目；该保险为自愿购买。

【住宿及其他資訊】
港澳台高校交流生住宿标准：預估 800 元/学期 (学期中通过网上支付平台进行缴费);
宿舍多为 6人/8人套间, 以及2人一房间, 房间配备空调, 套间内有独立卫浴; 宿舍楼提供公共洗衣机、烘干机; 电费由住宿人员均摊; 宿舍覆盖校园网, 需自行按月支付网络费用, 也可购买第三方运营商网络。
赴我校交流学习的贵校学生, 将另行通知选课、住宿、接送机、迎新等安排

【住宿資訊】
Not guaranteed but students can apply for housing. More information
here
. (P.12)
Students can either ask for a room in an on-campus residence (CROUS) or in a French host family through their online application form. Please be mindful of the fact that the number of rooms is limited.
Cost estimation:
Room in a residence: 1088€ (Fall semester) / 1630€ (Spring semester)
Room in a host family (including breakfasts and dinners in the workweek, and all meals during the weekend): 2000€ to 2600€ (Fall semester) / 3000€ to 3900€ (Spring semester)

【住宿資訊】
Accommodation is available, but cannot be guaranteed due to limited capacities. TU Darmstadt does not have its own dormitories but cooperates with other public providers in Darmstadt. Our colleagues from the
Exchange Students Housing Assistance ESHA
help incoming students find accommodation.
The typical accommodation we can offer is a single room (furnished with a bed, chair, table, and wardrobe) in a shared apartment in a student dorm. The rental period is six months (September to February, March to August) or five months (October to February, April to August). Monthly rent typically ranges between €400 and €600.

【住宿資訊】
Seezeit student services
is the largest provider of student accommodation in Konstanz. The rooms are usually in
single or double occupancy apartments
as well as in shared flats (WGs = Wohngemeinschaft). Every student, however, receives their own personal room. The WGs are usually shared by male and female students. Due to the extremely high demand, the rooms are assigned by lottery. The application for the dormitory room is part of the application for an exchange place at the University of Konstanz and is completed together.
Remember to transfer the deposit of
800€
to Seezeit. Only then can your application for a dormitory be considered.

【住宿資訊】
The International Office can arrange housing for exchange students from overseas in student dorms on request. Further information on how to apply online for student housing will be emailed to successful applicants.
The Studierendenwerk Stuttgart
is in charge of the allocation of the dormitory rooms. We do not have any influence concerning the location or the same price category of the allocated spaces.
You will have to
transfer the deposit of EUR 700 in advance
. Otherwise, your dorm room will be cancelled.
According to the regulations of the Studierendenwerk, students are required to book
a minimum rental period
: either
from
Sept. 1/March 1
(students who attend the intensive German course) or
from Oct. 1/April 1
(students who do not attend the intensive German course)
until Feb. 28/Aug. 31
(students who will stay for one semester). Students who will stay for two semesters will receive a rental contract for 11-12 months. Other periods of rental agreements are not possible!
Only in the case of
examinations in March or September
can your residence contract be extended by one month after the examination registration period.

【住宿資訊】
Finding accommodation in Hamburg: Studies: University of Hamburg
A limited number of rooms in student residences are available for incoming exchange students; rents vary (EUR 370–510). The housing application form provided by the exchange coordinator must be submitted by 15 June for the winter semester, by 15 December for the summer semester.
We recommend applying for a student residence hall, but incoming exchange students are free to search for accommodation on their own. Rents vary according to size and location, but are usually much higher than in residence halls.

【住宿資訊】
KIT reserves rooms in
student residences
for students from partner universities.
Accommodation is guaranteed
if students adhere to the application procedure and deadlines. Details are sent by email after admission to KIT.
The furnished single rooms cost between €250 and €350 per month and are rented for fixed lease periods:
October to March (winter semester)
and/or
April to September (summer semester)
. Please note that these rental periods are non-negotiable, and no alternative move-in or move-out dates are available.
Please note that accommodation prices on the private market are significantly higher than those in student dorms, and there is also a risk of scams. For this reason, we highly recommend applying for a room in a student dorm through us.
For students attending the
pre-semester German language course
(starting mid-September in the winter semester/mid-March in the summer semester), we recommend reserving accommodation in youth hostels, hostels, or Airbnb for the two weeks before the rental period of guaranteed rooms in the student residences. This must be arranged privately, as KIT unfortunately cannot assist with finding housing on the private market.
【住宿申請注意事項】
交換期間住宿由KIT Housing Office全權主責，且將根據全球各姊妹校的申請狀況做分配，恕無法保證安排到自己的第一順位房源。為避免造成姊妹校行政流程負擔並顧及其他同學權益，在租約（rental agreement）開立後即無法取消／放棄住宿資格，請特別留意。

【住宿資訊】
The private housing market in Heidelberg is very tight, and living in residence halls run by the Studierendenwerk is the most affordable and most convenient way of staying in Heidelberg as an exchange student.
Types of accommodation include:
single room sharing kitchen and bathrooms in groups of 2-4
single room in dormitories with kitchens and bathrooms on each floor
a small number of single apartments
Fees for residence halls: Approx. 250 - 570 € / Month; 450 € refundable deposit

【住宿資訊】
The
Accommodation Service
offers a variety of housing options, including dorms, shared apartments, and fully furnished single apartments. Availability runs from the beginning of September/October or March/April onwards. Costs range from about € 500 to € 1200 per month.
Since there has been a dramatic increase in demand for student housing, students wishing to use the Accommodation Service must apply online no later than December 10 or June 10, using the link above. Registration requests are processed on a
first-come, first-served basis
.
*根據歷屆交換生指出，FU有三種宿舍房型，有兩種是簽六個月的合約，另一種則是可以直接簽到一年的。若選擇前兩者，第二學期將無法直接從住宿組登記到宿舍，請往後欲申請宿舍的同學特別留意。

【住宿資訊】
The University of Athens runs a
Student Residence Complex
(FEPA/ΦΕΠΑ in Greek) on campus consisting of 4 buildings (A, B, C, D), which can house 1064 students.
In addition to student residences, there are various ways to find a flat in Athens, ranging from advertisements to agencies and digital services.
Most apartments are unfurnished, while those near the city centre are usually old or recently renovated. Rent costs don't include public utility services (electricity, water, heating, telephone line, and internet). There is also a typical extra cost, a
building fee
, which is shared with the tenants, for services such as cleaners, gardeners, elevator maintenance, electricity for shared building spaces, etc.
Renting an apartment requires signing a
lease contract
, which is necessary for establishing tenant rights and responsibilities.
More information here
.

【生活費與保險資訊】
Study in Hungary - Your costs of living
Students should arrange for appropriate health insurance in their home country. Those with chronic illnesses should take care to ensure that these, too, are covered by the health insurance. Students taking any medication regularly should make sure that they will have access to it during their stay in Hungary.
【住宿資訊】
While Corvinus University cannot offer on-campus (dormitory) accommodation, we do have a selected number of places that offer dormitory-like accommodation (checked by Corvinus staff members) at similar prices. Information on these will be sent out to all incoming students after the preliminary course registration period, well before their date of arrival. Information on what to keep in mind and check if arranging for accommodation individually will also be sent out to students.

【住宿資訊】
We strongly advise students to apply for accommodation through the International Office. Students can only start this process after their exchange application has been approved.
A handling fee of €250 per semester is required for this service. The number of rooms available is limited, accommodation cannot be guaranteed, and is assigned on a
first-paid, first-served basis
. Rental periods are fixed and cannot be adjusted to the student's arrival and/or departure dates.
Further information can be found
on our website
.

【生活費與保險資訊】
Insurance
Healthcare insurance
By law, everyone in the Netherlands, even if you are here for only one or two semesters, must have healthcare insurance for medical expenses. The type of healthcare insurance you need depends on your situation. Please check your current insurance to see if it covers your stay in the Netherlands and to what extent.
Liability insurance and household contents insurance
Make sure you are sufficiently insured for liability and household contents. More information can be found via
MyMaastricht
or
Study in Holland
.
Cost of Living
【住宿資訊】
We must strongly advise you to arrange this urgently because available student housing in Maastricht is
very limited
. We strongly advise you not to come to Maastricht if you have not found housing in or around the city before the start of the academic year. Should you come to Maastricht against our advice without having arranged housing, please know that UM cannot help you because UM itself does not offer student housing, and there are no online classes.
For more information, have a look at
UM Guesthouse
. Please take into account the mandatory introduction days and examination days when booking a room.

【住宿資訊】
Universities in the Netherlands do not own student housing. For new international Erasmus+ / Exchange students who meet the requirements, Utrecht University does offer a Reserved Accommodation Programme. This housing is reserved for new international UU students via organizations like SSH Short Stay. The housing offered through this programme is furnished and available for fixed rental periods only.
Be aware that finding housing via this programme is NOT guaranteed. The offers are limited and on
first come, first served basis
. You can find more information
on this page
.

【生活費與保險資訊】
Estimated living expenses
: On average, students will need at least €968 – €1338 per month. Also see
financial matters
. Please note that public transport is not free for exchange students, but discount cards are available.
All students are obliged to have
health insurance
to cover any medical costs incurred during their stay. We strongly recommend that students ensure they have medical insurance before their arrival. Students are also highly recommended to take out liability insurance to cover any accidental damage caused to other persons or property.
【住宿資訊】
Prospective students are advised to apply for housing in a very early stage, and to
pay the housing application fee (€285) as early as possible after application
. An application for housing can be submitted via the application portal as soon as their application for admission has been submitted. There is no need to await a decision on their application for admission to Leiden University. Once a student has reserved an accommodation via University Housing, the housing agency DUWO further coordinates the process.
Housing
through Leiden University cannot be guaranteed, we insist that students also seek housing via other routes. If a student needs to find housing independently Leiden University can give
advice and tips
. Please be informed that private housing can be expensive and is scarce.

【住宿資訊】
A limited number of places are available in the dormitories for exchange students. The majority of places are in double rooms with a shared bathroom and kitchen.
Students apply for accommodation through the online application form. The places are assigned on a "first-come, first-served" basis; therefore, it is important to apply as early as possible. Students who do not receive a place in a dormitory are offered assistance in finding a room or apartment to rent. For more information, please
check this website
.

【住宿資訊】
We strongly recommend you secure your housing before arriving in Madrid.
1) UC3M Residence Halls:
There are two residence halls in Getafe and one in Leganes. Although priority was previously given to full-year students, due to growing capacity, they are now increasingly able to accommodate semester students as well.
UC3M Residence Halls Information
2) Private Residence Halls
: Not affiliated with the UC3M but still very close to the Campus and already in use by many international partners.
Getafe:
LIV Student Getafe
MiCampus Getafe
Amro Getafe
Leganes:
MiCampus Leganés
3) Housing agencies
: The ones listed on our webpage are the ones the University has signed collaboration agreements with, so these are the ones we strongly recommend using, in case the students want to use their services to share an apartment in Madrid, Getafe, or Leganes, or request options other than living in a residence hall:
UC3M Housing Agencies

The Mobility and Reception Office does not provide any accommodation service directly. However, UPF is a member of the BCU, a public service that assists international students coming to Barcelona. It manages the
BCU Housing Service
with a wide range of flats and rooms to rent and information about student residence halls. UPF has direct agreements with
some residence halls
. More information check
here
.

Academic Calendar
(> Academic calendar)
It is divided in three terms: September – December | January – March | April – June
Each term consists of 10 weeks of classes and 2 weeks for the exams.
Orientation days are planned to welcome exchange students at the beginning of each term. Attendance to these sessions is compulsory.
*請特別留意該校為三學期制，115-2甄選錄取者交換期為該校Term2+Term3

【住宿資訊】
Linköping University does NOT guarantee accommodation for all their incoming exchange students. We do, however, have a limited number of rooms that we offer exchange students on a
first come, first served basis
. Students apply for these rooms by using the same application form as for your courses.
The rooms are located in student corridors, with shared kitchens/living room and within walking/biking distance from the University. They are furnished and have a monthly rent of approximately 4128-4955 SEK (~€365-440). A number of small studios are also available and have a monthly rent of approximately 5000 -6608 SEK (~€440-580).
If a student is not offered a room from the University, they will get instructions from the housing coordinator at Linköping University on how to search for accommodation on their own.
More information here
.

【住宿資訊】
Campus Rapperswil
:
The student hall of residence is conveniently located, just a five-minute bus ride from campus. Shared apartment of 3 or 6 rooms with exchange students. Current cost is CHF 680 per month. Application is submitted together with the student exchange application.
Campus Buchs:
No on-campus accommodation. Rooms in shared flats and private accommodation in or near Buchs, approx. CHF 400 - CHF 700 monthly.
Campus St.Gallen:
No on-campus accommodation. Rooms in shared flats and studios with other exchange students, CHF 550 - CHF 700 monthly. Application deadlines: 15 May/15 October.

All full year
non-European exchange students
from non-European partners are guaranteed a place in one of the residential colleges of the University if they apply for the programme by the deadline. Students opt for
college accommodation
on the application form. Students will be notified of their college via e-mail. The college will then contact the student with further details prior to arrival.
For a full list of prices and the different options please refer to
Undergraduate Residence Charges
. College prices include food (fully catered / part catered options only) and utility costs.

Unfortunately, we do not open our halls of residence to European Exchange or SEMP students, but we can provide guidance to these students on how to secure suitable housing off-campus.

details: 住宿無保證；保險、役男出境與註冊依官方要求。

【生活費與保險資訊】
Cost of Living
Students coming to Sussex for one semester must take out private medical insurance before travelling. The insurance must cover their time in the UK and provide cover if they intend to travel outside of the UK. This applies to EU/EEA nationals as EHIC cards are no longer valid in the UK.
Students coming to Sussex for the full academic year will pay the
healthcare surcharge as part of the visa application
. This permits students to access the National Health Service (NHS). However, students will need to pay for some services such as dental treatment, eye tests, and prescriptions. It is recommended that students take out adequate insurance to cover other health-related costs.
【住宿資訊】
Full Year applicants are guaranteed university accommodation if they apply by the 30 June deadline.
Autumn/Spring students are required to check our
Accommodation pages
for updates whilst we are confirming the arrangements.
Students will receive housing application instructions with their offer letters (or shortly after). Our Housing Office processes all applications and they will inform the students directly about their allocations. In order to confirm their room offer, students will be required to formally accept.
Allocations are subject to availability.

All students MUST ensure they have adequate personal insurance cover prior to traveling to the UK. The University of Manchester does not require that incoming exchange students purchase a specific insurance policy, nor do we have an institutional policy available for purchase. Students should source their own insurance according to their needs/personal circumstances.

Not guaranteed, but students can apply for housing.
Application for housing
is a separate, additional online process, which students must complete AFTER receiving their offer letter from us. Students should NOT reject any room offer they are made – they will not receive another offer.

Cost of Living
【住宿資訊】
A range of accommodation options is available at a variety of price points and locations close to each of our campuses. Our rooms are all single-occupancy and can be private en-suite rooms or shared bathroom rooms. Students can submit special requests, such as accessibility features, a quieter room, a single-gender or alcohol-free flat, and more.
An offer of accommodation is guaranteed for students coming to Southampton for a single semester only, provided they apply by the deadline. For students coming to Southampton for the full academic year, we cannot guarantee accommodation, but we try to prioritise your application where possible. Please see our accommodation website for details on how to apply:
Student accommodation | University of Southampton
Students who do not want to apply for university accommodation or are unsuccessful in their application will need to find private rented accommodation. The Students' Union provides guidance
here
.

【住宿資訊】
不保證住宿
，更多資訊請見
此連結
On-campus accommodation
Information about on-campus options can be viewed
here
.
Students do not require an offer for Exchange or Study Abroad to apply for on-campus accommodation
; there is no fee to apply. Once applications open, students can go to the website to register, and complete an application. During the application process students
must ensure they answer that they are a Monash Abroad applicant.
As rooms are limited and offered on a first-come, first-served basis, we recommend students apply as soon as possible.
Questions not answered on the website can be directed to
Monash Residential Services
.
Off-campus accommodation
If students choose to live off-campus, they can
receive assistance/advice
on searching for rental properties, setting up a share house, things to look out for before you sign a contract, an idea of comparable rental costs, how to budget, and how to get the essentials like internet, gas and electricity connected.

【住宿資訊】
不保證住宿
，更多資訊請見
此連結

此連結
Student Accommodation at Victoria University of Wellington is very competitive. This means that students may not be placed in one of their initial choices for accommodation.
Accommodation applications open on
1 August each year
, and we strongly recommend applying as soon as they open.
Students can apply for accommodation
before they have been nominated or accepted
into the exchange programme.
It is particularly competitive for students coming for a single exchange term during Trimester 1 (February start) at Victoria University of Wellington.
Mature students or students who have experience living away from home are advised to consider the self-catered halls of residence. All students over the age of 20 will be offered a self-catered hall only.
All questions regarding accommodation applications should be directed to the
Accommodation Service
. We do not process accommodation applications and therefore have no impact on processing times.

Term and assessment dates
【Course Information】
You can list more courses than you need credit for, but please make sure that you indicate
how many credits you need
, and
which courses are compulsory for your programme
. We will then liaise with the relevant academic departments.
*If you have not submitted any course requests (i.e. a completed learning agreement) your
application will not be processed.
Students will
only be allowed
to register for courses that they have been approved for.
*The final course registration will be completed during and after the orientation, but the application for courses must be submitted with the online exchange application.
You can however take fewer courses than you were pre-approved for. The final learning agreement must be signed by your home coordinator.
【Selecting Courses】
For general instructions on finding courses, please visit the
Course Information section
on our website.
Useful links in your search for courses are supplied in the above two documents, and will lead you to:
The
Online Yearbook and Faculty Websites
(Overview of Degree Programmes and Course Lists per Faculty,
which will lead you to the Departments' websites
)
The
Departments’ websites
can also be found under the university’s A – Z links
Please also be aware of the fact that approval for courses at Stellenbosch is done by a very strict process, and approval/disapproval is the discretion of the relevant academic department/s. Course approval/disapproval feedback will be communicated continuously until arrival at Stellenbosch University.
When selecting courses ensure that you complete your application with the corresponding course codes and module names.
For example: 11147 717 Fixed Internet Securities (Theory)
No timetable classes will be negotiated, it would be the student's responsibility to maintain their participation in the course selected.
